note: Round-29 planning sweep, part 2: ENSEMBLE SIZE / CAPACITY. Purpose: decide whether 'larger ensemble size per controller (es = 8, 16, ...)' is a direction the external record supports, given NeuLegion's operating point es = 4 with forceMin dimensions (see PLAN-round29.md P7 and docs/research/round29-ensemble-size.md). Three fronts: (a) how large an ensemble needs to be and what its size should scale with; (b) what more members cost and how to get many members cheaply; (c) whether diversity/member count is what buys skill. OR-noise (thousands of unrelated physics/vision hits) discarded per raw/README.md.

ensemble_size_theory.title: Linear Ensemble Sampling with Smaller Ensembles
ensemble_size_theory.why: The regret/exploration literature needs an ensemble of Theta(d log T) and identifies an intrinsic Omega(d) ensemble-size barrier; the paper narrows the log-horizon gap so SMALLER ensembles retain the guarantee. Reading for NeuLegion: the ensemble size is a function of the effective dimension of the problem, not a free 'bigger is better' dial.

ensemble_size_theory.title: Time-uniform accuracy of ensemble Kalman filters with localization
ensemble_size_theory.why: Proves the REQUIRED ensemble size depends on the effective rank of the initial covariance and the dimension of the unstable subspace, not on the ambient state dimension. A second, independent statement that ensemble size is set by the effective (not nominal) dimension.

ensemble_cost_and_efficiency.title: BatchEnsemble: An Alternative Approach to Efficient Ensemble and Lifelong Learning
ensemble_cost_and_efficiency.why: States the tradeoff NeuLegion faces verbatim: an ensemble's cost for training AND testing increases LINEARLY with the number of networks, 'which quickly becomes untenable'; their fix is a shared backbone with per-member rank-1 modulations. The template for many cheap members.

ensemble_cost_and_efficiency.title: Model soups: averaging weights of multiple fine-tuned models improves accuracy without increasing inference time
ensemble_cost_and_efficiency.why: The many-member benefit can be realised in WEIGHT SPACE at single-model inference cost. The cheap alternative to N-way prediction averaging.

ensemble_cost_and_efficiency.title: Trainable Weight Averaging: Accelerating Training and Improving Generalization
ensemble_cost_and_efficiency.why: Learns the averaging coefficients over a set of candidate weights in a reduced subspace - the principled version of 'combine the members, do not just average them'.

ensemble_cost_and_efficiency.title: Virtual neural networks: hundreds of souls in a body
ensemble_cost_and_efficiency.why: 'Virtual neural networks': keep the trainable PARAMETER count constant and scale only COMPUTATION; many virtual models share weights from a small set of physical models, giving ensembles of hundreds. The direct evidence that member count and parameter count are separable.

ensemble_cost_and_efficiency.title: FLAME: Condensing Ensemble Diversity into a Single Network for Efficient Sequential Recommendation
ensemble_cost_and_efficiency.why: Explicitly condenses ensemble-level diversity into ONE network - evidence that the value of an N-member ensemble can be had without N networks.

ensemble_cost_and_efficiency.title: Diffusion Distillation for Efficient Weather Ensembles
ensemble_cost_and_efficiency.why: Compresses a multi-step generative ensemble teacher into a single-step student that matches or surpasses the teacher - the 'the ensemble is a training signal, not a deployment cost' pattern.

ensemble_diversity_and_selection.title: Decorrelation Is Not Complementarity: Skill, Not Lineage, Governs Trusted-Monitor Ensembles
ensemble_diversity_and_selection.why: CENTRAL COUNTERWEIGHT: over 24 monitors spanning 9 pretraining lineages and a 29x skill range, minimising pairwise correlation is NOT the same as complementarity; the MEMBERS' SKILL governs whether the ensemble helps. Directly against 'more members -> more diversity -> more skill'.

ensemble_diversity_and_selection.title: Ensemble Diversity Optimization for Subjective Supervision
ensemble_diversity_and_selection.why: Learns ensemble COMPOSITION AND SIZE end-to-end (Gumbel-Softmax) with an explicit signed diversity regularizer tuned on validation data. The 'make the cardinality a learned/searched quantity, not a fixed constant' route.

ensemble_diversity_and_selection.title: Measuring consistency via ensemble margin and local prediction variability: Auditing decision systems in the presence of predictive multiplicity
ensemble_diversity_and_selection.why: Gives the measurement instruments: ensemble margin and local prediction variability for auditing predictive multiplicity. The readout an es-sweep should report.

ensemble_diversity_and_selection.title: Uncertainty quantification for trustworthy deep learning: Methods and measures
ensemble_diversity_and_selection.why: Survey scoped to ENSEMBLE-BASED and approximate-Bayesian UQ and the MEASURES used to summarise their outputs - the map of what to measure (and what not to over-claim) from a member pool.

ensemble_diversity_and_selection.title: Simple and Scalable Predictive Uncertainty Estimation using Deep Ensembles
ensemble_diversity_and_selection.why: The canonical deep-ensembles result (typical M ~ 5, diminishing returns in M): ensembles buy calibrated uncertainty, and diversity rather than per-member accuracy is the mechanism. The baseline scaling claim, already cited in docs/research/ensemble-evolution.md.
